audit.why: 51.08% over 1016 games with Rumble owning levels 2-3 and first item, and Vayne taking two items, matches both the chart and the text. This is the one matchup in my slice where Rumble is favoured and the file says so honestly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game spike says 'Tumble-into-invis means she can dodge your Electro-Harpoon and re-engage on her terms', stated unconditionally. Tumble grants no invisibility on its own — the stealth comes from Final Hour (R), which also cuts Tumble's cooldown, and Final Hour is on 100/85/70.
audit.why: It changes when the spike exists. Outside Final Hour she is a visible target Tumbling on a short cooldown; inside it she is a different champion. Treating the whole late game as permanently stealthed makes the player give up windows that are actually open.
audit.corrected: The two-item spike is real, but the stealth half of it only exists while Final Hour is running — 100s at rank 1. Between ultimates she is visible and killable.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (Final Hour: 'gains increased Attack Damage, Invisibility during Tumble, reduced Tumble cooldown'; cd 100/85/70)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (a) The early paragraph says Condemn 'will pin you into a wall and interrupt your Flamespitter channel'. Flamespitter is not a channel — Riot's text has it dealing damage in a cone for 3 seconds after the cast, so a knockback does not interrupt it; it moves you out of the cone's reach. (b) whys[0] says Vayne 'has no dash', while the same matchup calls Tumble her evasion three separate times. Tumble is a dash.
audit.why: Point 4 is the key point and (a) misprices the whole trade. If Condemn cannot cut the burn, then eating a Condemn mid-Flamespitter costs you position, not damage — and the correct response is to pre-place yourself away from terrain rather than to hold Q back waiting for her E.
audit.corrected: Condemn knocks you out of Flamespitter's cone; it does not stop the burn, which keeps ticking for its full 3 seconds. What Condemn actually threatens is the terrain stun. And Tumble is her dash — a 6-second one at rank 1, so she can dodge one harpoon, not both.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (Flamespitter: 'dealing magic damage in a cone for 3 seconds' — no channel flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Condemn is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in six places across both layers — 'Track Condemn before every trade', 'engage only on Condemn's cooldown' — and its cooldown is never given anywhere.
audit.why: An instruction to track a cooldown without the number is not actionable. Condemn is 20s at rank 1 falling to 12s at rank 5, which is a genuinely long window early and the reason Rumble owns levels 2-3.
audit.corrected: Condemn is 20s at rank 1. That is a long time to own the lane — it is the concrete reason the early spike exists.

audit.whatIsWrong: Several boilerplate strings in the full layer refer to Vayne as 'he': tradeGood and dosFull[1].d say 'double-E slow if he runs', and dontsFull[0].d says 'half his win condition is gone'.
audit.why: Not a mechanical error, but it is visible on the page and reads as untended template text in a matchup the user is otherwise being asked to trust.
audit.corrected: Same strings with the correct pronoun.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing records that Scrap Shield carries no displacement.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json emits 'Both sides carry displacement (Scrap Shield (W) vs Condemn (E))' here. Condemn does displace; Scrap Shield does not — Riot's text is a shield plus a move-speed burst. Only one side carries displacement.
audit.corrected: No edit made — flagged so the false symmetry is not written in.

edits.before: Vayne is a ranged carry with no wave-clear and a weak level 1 — use that. Walk Flamespitter at her from the first wave and establish that stepping up to CS costs her HP. She cannot punish you until she has Tumble-into-Condemn coordination, so level 1 is free harassment. At level 2 your double-Electro-Harpoon slow comes online: Q her into Danger Zone range, then fire both harpoon stacks to keep her in the cone. The key threat is her E — Condemn will pin you into a wall and interrupt your Flamespitter channel, so map the wall geometry before you commit. Never run at her with your back to terrain she can Condemn you into.
edits.after: Vayne is a ranged carry with no wave-clear and a weak level 1 — use that. Walk Flamespitter at her from the first wave and establish that stepping up to CS costs her HP. She cannot punish you until she has Tumble-into-Condemn coordination, so level 1 is free harassment. At level 2 your double-Electro-Harpoon slow comes online: Q her into Danger Zone range, then fire both harpoon stacks to keep her in the cone. Condemn does not stop Flamespitter — the burn runs its full 3 seconds — it knocks you clear of the cone, and stuns only if you hit terrain. Condemn is 20s at rank 1; that gap is your lane.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are false positives. The real finds: (1) 'Condemn will ... interrupt your Flamespitter channel' — Flamespitter is not a channel, it burns for 3 seconds after the cast, so Condemn costs you position rather than damage, which changes how the trade is priced; (2) whys[0] asserts Vayne 'has no dash' while three other lines in the same matchup call Tumble her evasion; (3) Condemn is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in six places across both layers and its 20s rank-1 value appears nowhere; (4) 'Tumble-into-invis' is stated unconditionally though the stealth comes from Final Hour. Also worth the user's attention: tradeGood and two dos/donts strings call Vayne 'he' — that boilerplate is shared, so the same pronoun bug likely appears in other Rumble matchups against female champions.
